title: Stationary points, optimisation and inflexion

points.text: Points of inflexion with zero and non-zero gradient

bigPicture: Stationary points are where f′ = 0; testing tells maximum from minimum. Optimisation turns a worded problem into one function to maximise or minimise.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find and classify stationary points?
keyIdeas.answer: Solve f′(x) = 0; then check the sign of f′ either side, or f″: f″ > 0 minimum, f″ < 0 maximum, f″ = 0 inconclusive.
+ to −: maximum; − to +: minimum; no change: stationary inflexion.
Define variables, use the constraint to write one function of one variable, differentiate, set = 0, justify max/min, answer the question in context.
Where concavity changes: f″ changes sign. If f′ = 0 too it is a stationary inflexion; otherwise non-stationary.

misconceptions.right: Need a sign change in f″ (e.g. x⁴ at 0 is a minimum).

misconceptions.wrong: Giving x when asked for the maximum value

practice.prompt: An open box has a square base side x and volume 32 cm³. Find x minimising the outer surface area.
f(x) = x e^(−x/2), x ≥ 0. Use the GDC to find the maximum point and the non-stationary inflexion point.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
